An online ecospace makes TTRPGs more of a disposable commodity. In physical games you need to make the effort of turning up in person, which means more of a commitment. You cannot convince them to do that. They refuse. Dead-ass refuse.

It became increasingly more difficult for new players to look at a drawing of two vampires across two spreads and say "That's a Ventrue and that's a Setite" or "That's a Gangrel and that's an Assamite".  It just isn't as, well, iconic.
These images were great at-a-glance representations which, by the time we got to 5th edition, all very much became homogenized into a 'generic person unremarkable clothing' style.

Contentiously, I think these otherwise wonderfully accessible and recognisable spreads kinda dropped off as the game went on, with the biggest victim being the art piece which was often central for new players to get a good sense of recognition for who the clan's core identity was.

One of the best things early WoD games would do was these; 2-page spreads per Clan/Tribe which gave the players an at-a-glance understanding of the clan type, with text details, outlines of their personalities and attitudes, and an iconic artpiece.
I would argue that it already has collapsed, but there is so much money involved in such large companies that the collapse was just not as visible or obvious.
It's not often that I recommend a game which I feel has real, genuine soul to it. Check out 'Our Brilliant Ruin' and give it a shot!

Writing a book is an accomplishment.
Building an author career takes endurance.

One is putting words on the page.
The other is pushing past setbacks, self-doubt, and wondering if anyone will read it.

If you’re still writing through it all, you’re doing the part most people never see.💙

#AuthorSky
It definitely is torment especially after you work hard to promote and get reviews only for Amazon to take the reviews away that are verified purchased reviews.
Just DM’d you. Always love chatting and supporting fellow authors. It's easier to chat there. 🙂
It still ongoing and there is no help with available since Amazon has ZERO author support.

I’m not getting into details, but the past 2 weeks dealing with Amazon issues nearly pushed me to quit. It’s not even writing the book. It’s everything after that tests you.

Some platforms make this journey harder than it should be.

Quitting would be easier. That’s exactly why I won’t.

#AuthorSky

text:
What if there was a Black Mirror episode about authors where AI decides what’s allowed to exist & what gets erased.

Social policing marks strangers as “connections” & punishes them.

Friendships become data points. Every digital footprint is watched.

Oh wait. This isn’t an episode.

#AuthorSky
It's been one of the hardest 2 weeks in publishing I’ve experienced. Trying not to quit. It's easier to give up then to fight through it.

In publishing, some setbacks don’t just sting, they hit deep. They can mess with your head, your confidence, everything.

I’m going through one right now. It’s harder than I expected.

If you’re in it too, don’t let it take you out.

#AuthorSky #HealthSky

Waiting for perfection can keep a book unfinished forever. Sometimes the real progress is letting the book be imperfect, finishing the story, and trusting revision later.

The goal isn’t perfection. It’s getting the story told.

#AuthorSky #BookSky

It's great that you got an advance. I am with a small press and there isn't one. I have an author friend that was published by a big indie that gets distribution by one of the Big 5 and they didn't get much marketing help either.
Definitely! I used to think oysters were disgusting when I was younger and now I love oysters! 🦪
3k is really good! I've found FB ads to work better than Amazon ads if you plan on doing them.
You actually need back surgery?

Some books don’t find their readers right away. Timing, visibility, and word of mouth all matter—and sometimes the right readers show up months or even years later.

A slow start doesn’t mean the story failed.

#AuthorSky #BookSky
Very true and that goes for musicians too

Most “overnight success” in publishing isn’t overnight at all. It’s years of writing, rewriting, rejection, quiet releases, and showing up long before anyone notices.

The success people see is usually just the part that finally became visible.

#AuthorSky
Sorry to hear. I hope it gets better.
Haha…BIC-HOK exactly!
Definitely, it usually always begins fun. Over time, we have to tap into resilience and consistency especially during revisions.
Very true about anything hard.

People think writers wait for inspiration, but most books get written on tired days, bad days, and days you’d rather quit.

On the days you don’t feel creative. On the days the words fight you. On the days showing up feels harder than writing itself.

Books get finished by discipline.

#AuthorSky
Thank you and same here. I enjoyed Leo’s backstory quite a bit and the reveal of his present identity.

Sobriety isn’t just about quitting something. It’s about learning to stay.

To sit in the present instead of constantly trying to escape it. To face yourself clearly. To build a life you don’t need to run from.

Maybe that’s why writing feels different now because honesty does.

#AuthorSky #SoberSky

I prefer now to not have family or loved ones (unless they are objective avid readers) read my work. Cause I think strangers are more honest and I appreciate that more.

Yeah, I know what was stated and my post is not about gifting or expectations. It is specifically about family not wanting to read author books. It isn’t about gifting it is about support and where it comes from. Usually from strangers which I actually prefer since family could be subjective.

There is an audience for every genre and that audience is often times not our family. I write thrillers with a romance b-story and a family member said they wouldn’t read my book cause they read mysteries with romance in them. I was like…uh…okay.
I learned that lesson quick. All my support have come from people I’ve never met.

Yeah that is another thing. Reminds me of the mom who convinces their kid that they’re great singers and good enough to try out for American Idol only to make their 5 seconds of fame in the blooper segment as some of the worst singers that have ever tried out for the show. 🤣

As authors we’re told to build our audience & to start with friends & family. 

But many won’t buy the book, won’t read it, & won’t review it, even when gifted a copy. You can’t rely on those closest to you. 

For many of us, most of our support will come from total strangers.

#AuthorSky #BookSky
Oh totally. I think it relates to most art where there are genre categories and it is super subjective.

Yeah, that’s a big one. I tried reading an indie book where the paragraphs were very long and none were indented. I couldn’t get through it. Non-standard formatting pulls me out of the story. I don’t mind POV changes in the same chapter if they’re executed well and separated with asterisks.

Yeah, I always give every genre a chance cause I love to read and try not to judge based on genre. I try to support indie authors too. My only requirement is that it is formatted correctly & mostly error-free. Though as long as the errors aren’t major, excessive & distracting I’ll give it a chance.

Same. Got rejected by my own family member who said they would not read my thriller book that has a romance b-story cause she likes mysteries with romance?! I’m like…huh??

I’ve had more support from strangers and have been more successful partnering up with genre specific newsletter outreach.

I’m not a big large-world sci-fi person either cause it’s often hard to remember a massive world and all the rules. But Blake Crouch’s Dark Matter was a genre blend and super easy to follow. But when they turned it into a tv series, the show made it harder to follow. I preferred the book.

Same here. I don’t have triggers & I’m not picky. I read everything cause I’ve learned so much by keeping an open mind. My favorite books:

-Silver Lining Playbook (dramedy)
-Dark Matter (sci-fi)
-The Shining (horror)
-The Book Thief (ya/historical)
-Anything from Harlan Coben (thriller)

So very true. So many tastes out there, preferences, and pickiness. When it comes to books I see it as art and have read every genre and genre blend under the sun. But I know not everyone is like that.

As an author & multi-genre reader, I know not every genre is for everyone.

Some can’t handle murder in the news, let alone in thrillers. Some want romance, not details. Some find real life scary & avoid horror. Others escape into fantasy.

Find your audience. They’re out there.

You can find display options on display2go.com Note: the price for the display is reasonable - shipping is $$ so try to do a group of displays and share shipping for best deals. #displays #writingcommunity #booksky #basicmarketing #becomeavailable #sellingnovels

Basically, this display box is cardboard and holds many books. It is the type of box you find in large bookstores when a book or series is being promoted. You make up large sticker sheets of printed art and stick them to the display. Fiddly. Cool.

#writingcommunity #booksky #displays #stickers

I have a friend stopping by today. We are going to build a display box for next weekend's writing group. I have a demo for how to build and use a simple display in your local area. Putting your work before the public requires efforts by you for you.

#writingcommunity #booksky #displays #stickers

Identifying how important your written works are to you will be revealed under the pressure of supporting your works. Free and easy is where most writers start. They can stop any time. Unless maybe they can't. Only you can decide how important your writing is.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writing

Are you spending your marketing money on a fancy morning coffee? Do you buy shoes with your closet full of shoes? Do you have lots of auto payments for apps and services you don't need? Do you say yes to your impulse spending. That's your marketing budget.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing

Look at your current cash flow, what you are spending money on and why. How can you carve out saving for your novel support? What are your poor financial habits? You may feel confronted by unexamined behaviors. It's time to be intentional and in choice.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing #money
True!!!

Learned helplessness is real. This is where you don't try to help yourself. You believe you have no options. You believe in your failure as a self-fulfilling prophesy. Bullocks. It's 'learned' which means you can overwrite learned helpfulness. Take actions.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing

Once you make the decision to assist your own novel your perspective will begin to shift. In the midst of all of this you will be fighting your imposter syndrome which likely tells you that you aren't good enough. This is grooming. Stand up anyway.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing #imposter

The publishing process of 50 years ago no longer functions today. Stop waiting to be discovered. In today's world you need to empower yourself around your writing. You need to seek out editors. You need to buy the help you need that years past was funded.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing

Learning how to value your writing is a huge deal. You have been groomed to wait for received validation from strangers. The 'waiting' process for writers is legendary and difficult to navigate. Your life is short. You have to sluff off this waiting process.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing

You don't need to know how to market today. You start by knowing you need a budget for marketing. That's it. You achieve a budget by saving for it. You tell your family and friends to shift any gifts to this support via cash. Be serious. Money doesn't magically appear.

#writingcommunity #booksky

Create the habit of supporting your novel.

You are the founding patron of your written works. You have to believe first. You believe by taking the ACTIONS of support. Words aren't enough. Being cheap won't cut it. Decide you are worth it. I know it's scary.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing

For a short time you can trade your 'time' for money at the start of your career. But, this grace period is short and you need to decide to help your novels succeed. Wrap your mind around saving the money for you to spend on marketing later. You will need it.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing

The first big obstacle of your writing success is your familiar villain, Imposter Syndrome. 

We talk a lot about IS here because it plagues most writers and shows up  lurking around every corner. Today, open a savings account and create a fan funnel.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing #money

You can use an app like Linktree for a free email collector form. FREE! Other sites also offer these. No excuses. Set up your fan funnel today and save a QR code for it and save the url for it. Post these so people check them out and sign up. You need fans.

#writingcommunity #booksky #fanfunnels

The second factor in your writing career success is fans. Fans push the sales algorithms on websites where books are sold.

At minimum, you need a fan funnel today. This is an online form that sends you email addresses of fans. It can be free to create.

#writingcommunity #booksky #fanbase #fans

For many writers as they publish several novels the money they save will become circulating money. Their profits will rise fueled by the marketing that is ongoing. You may not be an expert at marketing and may need to hire experts. Be ready.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing #money

So we start our career building by deciding to save money for our career building. I recommend a minimum of $100 per week but if you are skint, save some amount, you can build up along the way. Expect to do this for years. You won't just write one book.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing #money

The first understanding of the writer is that you control what you do or don't do to help the sales of your novels. It is fundamentally a decision on your part. Marketing costs money. To be able to market means you save money for a budget.

#writingcommunity #booksky #marketing #money #novelsales

Good Morning Monday People!!!

Mondays are all about money. A writer moving toward success is almost certain to be engaging in marketing. This may range toward only free types of posts, all the way up to larger advertising. Money. Marketing is $$$

#writingcommunity #booksky #money #marketing

Does the write 'land' their story?

This is a critical factor for the writer. They have to tell their story in such a way that the reader accepts the story for its premise. In this way the story has the maximum impact on delivery. Landing stories is hard.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writinglife

When we pick up a book we fundamentally understand that what we will read is SHAPED intentionally by a writer. This means that book is a narrative. Some claim pure facts and they may be right, but they didn't include all facts only some. #writingcommunity #booksky #narrative #facts #writing

Exactly! Many writers struggle with UR. A novel is a narrative intended to entertain, inform or persuade the reader. In a novel the writer collects a select group of fictitious events that necessarily include the bias of the selections. #writingcommunity #booksky #narratives #characters #writing

The author of a novel should feel solid to the reader, they feel they are in good hands with a writer who knows what they are doing.

Being a trustworthy author who writes unreliable characters is tricky. Maintain your autonomy. Deliver good characters.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writinglife

The narrator in a novel is NOT the author. 

Why is your character unreliable? Generally, this is due to:

* youth
* mental illness
* trauma
* drugs
* malice
* lack of experience

At the same time the unreliable narrator is engaging causing the reader to go along.

#writingcommunity #booksky #write

A reliable and unreliable narrator both lie to the reader. A novel is not true. What the reader needs is the belief that the writer can deliver on great story. Choosing an unreliable narrator is simply a bit more advanced or difficult to deliver. Be careful!

#writingcommunity #booksky #unreliable

Not 10 minutes after the shooting event last night, people were talking false flag.

This is what lack of trust creates. As a writer you must build trust with your readers and maintain that trust, it's not that you won't lie to them, you will...

#writingcommunity #booksky #trustissues #writing

A sample book will inform you on the correct arrangement of pages for your front matter. It will show you good font sizes, leading, margins. Try not to cut corners. Readers have been groomed to how a book should feel when done right. Design is a skill.

#writingcommunity #booksky #formatting #novels

A well-designed book doesn't have headers in the front matter. Most generic template have issues with this and it is fussy to eliminate what you don't want. When you are planning to format a book, find the BEST trad published sample book you can find.

#writingcommunity #booksky #samplebooks

The books I am formatting today (versus years ago) are done in Affinity 2. However, I had to create a modified dual template to meet my needs. This means the template is specific for printing two-up. This is what I wanted. The program is designed for regular format.

#writingcommunity #booksky

If you are new to typesetting and formatting you need to start off knowing you will have mistakes. Try not to set yourself up with a tight time limit as all the programs have fiddly, glitchy bits. Patience and an eye for detail are critical. Readers will notice.

#writingcommunity #booksky #format

When you are stuck, change things.

By moving away from your normal novel writing and going into construction questions, you force your brain to look at the situation from a different rut. Something is wrong and finding what it is requires investigation.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writinglife

It is common to rush things in a novel. It is common to add in too much exposition and bore the reader to snores too. Your writing style can unfortunately include both of these at the same time creatine writing lurch. Pacing is learned. You will have a natural to you pace.

#writingcommunity #books

If your crises are compressed in your actual timeline pushing you toward a too-short-for-market novel, then you need to understand this as it is likely to change your process. Knowledge helps you. Your novel should hit the right notes for readers.

#writingcommunity #booksky #novelproblems #timing

When you read your comps on Thursdays and gather your book data, you can gather the story arc too. You can pinpoint where each story crisis falls in that novels timeline. You can identify word count to crisis point to show the data details clearly.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writingproblems

On your hallway wall timeline paper you should be able to plot your story arc on its own line. What are the crisis points? How big are they? How many more do you need to the big one? You can see your pacing at the same time. This points to your speed and style.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writing

There are 7 basic common types of story structures. A review will take you around an hour. When you identify the one you are using, that will give you insight into your location within that structure. Are you supposed to be on the clackety clack of the roller coaster?

#writingcommunity #booksky

It is perfectly fine to review things you learned about story structure years ago in some classroom. You will forget. If you are in the sag there is likely some forgotten understanding happening. Surf around for story arcs and see what kind you are working with.

#writingcommunity #booksky #storyarc

A novel is like a road trip. You can get lost. When you map the rise and falls within your 'trip' you can find out where you are within the general structure of the story arc. This can help you understand what needs to happen next for your novel.

#writingcommunity #booksky #storyarc #writinglife

If you are stuck in your novel, in the saggy middles, and you are problem solving to get things moving again, take some time to draw out your timeline and map your story arc. Where are you in your necessary crises within the novel? What structure are you using?

#writingcommunity #booksky #crises
It's so worth it!

You want to be able to see how your novels fit into the meta timeline with your time date stamps. A meta timeline can span a year or generations depending on your story. You need to get it right. You need to be consistent across novels. This is work.

#writingcommunity #booksky #timelines #spans

I find the easiest timeline is a long sheet of kraft paper taped to that longest hallway wall in your house. On that paper draw a meta timeline line. Then a line for each novel. Note you may have another bigger timeline for that novel already. 

#writingcommunity #booksky #timelines #wallart

I know you think you will remember. Doh. This is a now or later situation. You do it now or later. If later, you will be neck deep in the next story and already have far too much to correct because you are lazy now. A novel series will require you to make a timeline.

#writingcommunity #booksky

In your glossary you identify everything you talk about or even hint about in your novel. You create a map glossary laying out the places you mention, their distances, their terrain. You won't remember all of this fresh. A series will trip you up.

#writingcommunity #booksky #series #novels #write

The moment you get your first hint that your standalone novel may be a novel in a series, you are in trouble. Create a novel series glossary file. This file correctly spells name and then writes a short bio for that name with age, height, coloring, scars etc.

#writingcommunity #booksky #glossaries

You won't remember.

You are today years old before you fully understand that when you create whole new worlds, you won't remember or retain the details. You may even find you forget you wrote that novel entirely. This isn't bs, you have storage problems.

#writingcommunity #booksky #writingnovels
